29: MATRYÓNA. Four of 'em. What decent girl would have him! Well, so he's taken her, and she's glad. You see, the vessel was not sound, so the wine trickled out.
28: NEIGHBOUR. He's a widower. I suppose there are children?
25: MATRYÓNA. Ah, now if it were a poor man, then, as the saying is, it's always unseasonable for a poor man to marry. But it's Simon Matvéyitch, he's married that Marína.
22: MATRYÓNA. Yes, you had better. And we've had a wedding down in our parts.
18: MATRYÓNA [ sitting down ] Yes, it's true, I'm quite done up, my dears. As to extreme unction, that's absolutely necessary. Besides, they say it's good for the soul.
17: ANÍSYA. Ploughing. But you come in and we'll get the samovár ready; the tea'll set you up again.
16: MATRYÓNA. Ah, but a widow's lot is also bitter. It's all right as long as one's young, but who'll care for you when you're old? Oh yes, old age is not pleasure. Just look at me. I've not walked very far, and yet am so footsore I don't know how to stand. Where's my son?
15: NEIGHBOUR. Yes, that's true, dying for a year, it's no joke. You're bound hand and foot like that.
14: ANÍSYA. Yes, if it were only over one way or other!
13: NEIGHBOUR. Oh, Anísya dear, I should think your heart must be heavy. As the saying goes, “Not he is sick that's ill in bed, but he that sits and waits in dread.”
12: ANÍSYA. The neighbours advise it. If he lives till to-morrow we'll send for the priest.
11: MATRYÓNA. Well, and is he to have extreme unction?
10: ANÍSYA. He came to, and creeps about again.
8: NEIGHBOUR. I had a look at him yesterday. Dearie me! one wonders his body and soul keep together. And, O Lord, the other day he seemed just at his last gasp, so that they laid him under the holy icóns. [1] They started lamenting and got ready to lay him out.
6: ANÍSYA. Oh dear yes, the priest was here yesterday.
5: ANÍSYA. Where's the hurry? MATRYÓNA. Well, and has he had communion?
3: NEIGHBOUR. Yes, that's always so. [ To Anísya ] And I was thinking of beginning to bleach the linen, but it is a bit early, no one has begun yet.
1: MATRYÓNA. Straight from home, dear. Come to see my son. Brought him some shirts—can't help thinking of these things, you see, when it's one's own child.
0: NEIGHBOUR [ approaches Matryóna ] How do you do, granny? Have you come far?
